meta.scope: Selected funded projects and competition editions directly relevant to gait identity recognition or related whole-body and cross-camera matching.
meta.selection: Primary grant records, government or institutional reports, organizer websites and competition reports. Health-only, rehabilitation-only and procurement projects are excluded.
meta.yearRule: Years match documented project intervals or competition editions. Records with only a launch or solicitation year match that year; this is not an active-project calendar.

records.title: DARPA HumanID
records.host: DARPA / US Army · Southampton gait research
records.summary: Supported early gait biometrics for identifying people at a distance, including model-based and appearance-based analysis of walking video.
records.details: The Southampton account documents a HumanID-funded gait-recognition award and subsequent development of gait biometrics. HumanID is a historical research program, distinct from the annual HID competition series that began in 2020.

sources.label: Institutional record
sources.evidence: Underpinning research and reference 3.1 identify the Southampton award and its period.

records.title: BRIAR
records.host: IARPA · Biometric Recognition and Identification at Altitude and Range
records.summary: Develops whole-body biometric identification at long range and from elevated platforms, combining gait, body shape and face evidence.
records.details: The program describes imaging at 300+ meters, elevated sensor angles of at least 20 degrees, and atmospheric turbulence. Its scope includes detection, tracking, biometric signature extraction and multimodal matching. These are program scenarios, not accuracy claims.

sources.label: Program overview
sources.evidence: The official summary specifies the November 2021 launch, sensing scenarios and whole-body/face fusion.

records.title: Video LINCS
records.host: IARPA · Video Linking and Intelligence from Non-Collaborative Sensors
records.summary: Studies object re-identification across heterogeneous cameras and localization in a common reference frame, including aerial–ground video association.
records.details: People and vehicles are initial object classes. The program also studies broader object matching and geo-localization without prior knowledge of collection geometry. This is related cross-camera association research; gait identification is not the program’s sole or stated mandatory biometric.

sources.label: Program overview
sources.evidence: The official summary defines the re-identification task; the solicitation was released on May 21, 2024.

records.title: Adaptive-resolution LiDAR for person recognition
records.host: JSPS KAKENHI · Osaka University · Yasushi Yagi
records.summary: Studies LiDAR optics, resolution allocation and person-recognition methods, with related work on gait identification and 3D human representations.
records.details: Project 22H00538, Grant-in-Aid for Scientific Research (A), addresses limited spatial resolution in distant person sensing. Listed outputs include human-mesh gait recognition and a large-population gait database with human meshes. The project covers identity and attribute recognition, rather than gait alone.

records.title: HID 2026
records.host: International Joint Conference on Biometrics (IJCB)
records.summary: Uses SUSTech-Competition silhouettes with reference code, automated Codabench evaluation and stricter restrictions on use of earlier test probes.

One sequence per identity forms the gallery; remaining sequences form probes, released in 10% and 90% phases. Top submissions undergo code-based reproducibility checks. records.title: OUMVLP-OF Gait Recognition Challenge
records.host: International Joint Conference on Biometrics (IJCB)
records.summary: Evaluates optical-flow gait identification and verification using versions with retained or removed background information.
records.details: V1 retains background in optical-flow maps; V2 masks it using silhouettes. Identification uses rank-1 and verification uses equal error rate. The later official update supplies training samples, superseding the earlier no-training-data statement still present on the page.

sources.label: Official challenge
sources.evidence: The dataset section describes V1/V2 and the training-data update; the tracks specify rank-1 and EER.
